title: Viper Image That Caused Alarm in California Was A.I.-Generated

reading.body:
This is a case of a fabricated image being treated as photographic evidence of a sighting and acted on as though it were real. The picture offered as proof that a Gaboon viper was in a residential neighborhood had been generated by artificial intelligence, and the official response followed from it.

The failure sits at the intake of a public report, at the point where an image is accepted as a record of something that happened. Nothing in the account shows the image was checked for provenance before the alert was issued and a search was mounted. Establishing where the image came from, or whether it depicted a real scene, before treating it as evidence would have been the step that caught it.

What is not established is who generated the image or why. The reporting shows the image was AI-generated and the sighting report false, and it does not establish an intent to cause alarm.

reports.title: Viper Image That Caused Alarm in California Was A.I.-Generated

summary:
Santa Ana police in Southern California warned residents on Monday that a Gaboon viper had been seen in a tree in a residential neighborhood. The snake was estimated to be four to five feet long. Police said it was highly venomous and told people not to approach or handle it. The report caused alarm because Gaboon vipers normally live in the rainforests of equatorial Africa. Police called in herpetologists and searched the area, but they did not immediately find the snake.

The image offered as evidence of the sighting turned out to be fake. It had been generated by artificial intelligence. The police alert and the search were based on a false report. No snake or evidence of it was found.
